issues.description: Automated mutation analysis flags SR2 as a 'dead check' (check_activation shows no isolated SR2-only FAIL across the mutant suite) even though the differential run against the naive baseline submission clearly shows SR2 failing correctly (coverage 0.00 below threshold). This suggests the mutant set lacks a targeted SR2-only mutant to confirm discriminative power in isolation, though the mechanism itself appears functionally correct.
issues.evidence: dead_checks: ["SR2"] while differential.vulnerable_run.stdout shows '[TEST] FAIL: SR2: coverage 0.00 below required threshold 0.66'

issues.description: No mutants were generated/run that specifically target FR3 (invalid node name reference) or FR4 (short summary), leaving those functional requirements formally untested by the mutation suite even though their code paths are present and appear correct on manual review.
issues.evidence: untested_requirements: ["FR3", "FR4"]; per_requirement_coverage shows FR3 and FR4 covered:false, mutants_targeting:0

recommendations: Add at least one mutant that only breaks FR3 (e.g., invents a non-existent net name in suspect_nodes) and one that only breaks FR4 (e.g., truncates summary below 20 chars) to close the FR3/FR4 mutation coverage gap.

Investigate and resolve the discrepancy between check_activation (which shows SR2 count of 0) and the differential vulnerable_run (which shows SR2 FAIL firing correctly) — likely a mutant-suite bookkeeping issue rather than a grader defect, but should be reconciled for a clean validation report.
Once FR3/FR4-targeted mutants and the SR2 dead-check discrepancy are addressed, re-run validation to confirm overall_status can be upgraded to pass.
